definitions.gloss: to hold one's breath; to stop breathing
definitions.explanation: To intentionally stop breathing for a period of time. Used both literally (swimming, medical procedures) and figuratively (in tense or exciting moments).

examples.english: I held my breath before diving underwater.

examples.japanese: ⟦{観客|かんきゃく}→観客：02556_kankyaku⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{息|いき}を{止|と}めて⟦{結果|けっか}→結果：02486_kekka⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見守|みまも}った→見守る：04574_mimamoru⟧。
examples.english: The audience held their breath as they watched for the result.

examples.japanese: ⟦レントゲン→レントゲン：11219_rentogen⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{撮|と}る→撮る：00760_toru⟧とき、⟦{技師|ぎし}→技師：02680_gishi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧「{息|いき}を{止|と}めて⟦ください→ください：02899_kudasai⟧」⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{言|い}われた→言う：00515_iu⟧。
examples.english: When getting the X-ray, the technician told me, 'Please hold your breath.'

notes:
Used both for the literal physical action of holding one's breath and figuratively for moments of intense suspense or concentration. The figurative use often describes an audience or observer watching something tense unfold.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {息|いき}を{止|と}めて⟦ください→ください：02899_kudasai⟧: please hold your breath (medical/photography instructions)
- {息|いき}を{止|と}めて⟦{見守|みまも}る→見守る：04574_mimamoru⟧: to watch with bated breath

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{息|いき}を{呑|の}む→息を呑む：06902_ikiwonomu⟧: to gasp, to be breathtaken — describes an involuntary reaction to something stunning or shocking
- ⟦{息|いき}→息：02176_iki⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{殺|ころ}す→殺す：01944_korosu⟧: to hold one's breath (to hide) — implies suppressing breathing to avoid being detected
- ⟦{息|いき}→息：02176_iki⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{吸|す}う→吸う：04394_suu⟧: to breathe in, to inhale — the simple act of inhalation
